population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The 328 member fare is a strong, affordable trigger for a spontaneous solo break I have been keen to arrange after six months without leisure travel. Komatsu has medium appeal and I am open to any served destination, so this cheap offer turns casual browsing into a worthwhile trip. I would still pay the 410 normal fare if the member quota runs out.

analysis.summary: Eight of sixteen members bought at the 328 HKD fare, citing it as a compelling bargain; several said they would also pay the 410 HKD regular fare. Six declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and one decline reflected low trip interest and recent travel, not price. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to strong value at the current fare, but buying at 328 does not prove willingness to pay more, and the fare sits at the permitted cap.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher fare is precluded by the cap, so test whether the current 328 HKD fare sustains conversion on fresh members; if paired conversion falls materially below the observed ~50%, the value-driven interpretation is contradicted.

analysis.summary: Eight of sixteen members bought at the 328 HKD fare, citing it as a compelling bargain; several would also pay the 410 regular fare. Six declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), not price objections. Two declines were low-interest optional browsing despite finding 328 affordable. No inventory denials occurred and capacity was not binding, so the environment-forced declines reflect budget mismatch rather than price rejection. Evidence supports testing the same fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 328 HKD member fare on fresh members will yield conversion at or above the observed 51%, with most declines attributable to budget or low interest rather than fare level. A materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 328 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 members bought and 9 declined. Six declines cite low trip interest or weak destination appeal with a strong outside option, not the fare itself; three are environment-forced inventory denials. Price is mentioned as affordable by most decliners, and several buyers say the fare itself triggered booking. The cap is already reached, so no higher test is permitted. Evidence points to holding the fare while testing on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 328 HKD member fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly 38% weighted conversion; if a paired fresh sample shows materially lower conversion with no change in inventory denials, the hold direction is contradicted.

Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at HK$255 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh paired customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts versus HK$255, because most current buyers named the fare as a bargain and many accepted the HK$410 fallback. A significant revenue drop would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 328 HKD member fare, 5 of 16 customers bought the member ticket, all citing the fare as compelling value, and several said they would still pay the 410 regular fare. Nine declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest optional-trip declines, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. Evidence points to testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at today's fare does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at least as high as at 328 HKD, since current buyers report the fare as compelling and several state willingness to pay the 410 regular fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 328 HKD member fare, six of sixteen customers bought and ten declined. Five declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; the other five declined for low trip interest or strong outside options despite calling the fare affordable. Buyers repeatedly cited the 328 fare as a bargain versus the 410 normal fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high, so the evidence does not support lowering price; the fare is already at its permitted cap, so a higher test is unavailable.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 328 HKD fare on fresh members will yield a similar conversion, with declines driven mainly by low trip interest or unavailable inventory rather than fare level; a materially higher share of explicit price objections would contradict this.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Independent validation is read once after freezing the selected tested price; no refitting on holdout.

person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Browsing the route network without choosing a destination; an unusually attractive basic fare is the reason to consider travelling at all.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The destination is interchangeable. Compare the ticket's appeal with keeping the money, not with a need to reach this particular city.
person.outside_option: Make no booking now and stay open to another destination later; no cheaper future fare is guaranteed.
person.motivation_context: Only browsing for inspiration; another optional trip is not currently a priority. Returned from a leisure trip within the last two weeks. This destination is particularly appealing today, although another destination could also work. Keeping the schedule free and retaining the ticket money is a strongly appealing alternative.

decision.reason: No offered ticket is both available and within my basic-fare budget.

person.segment_label: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Open to a short break if the offer makes it worthwhile, without a committed itinerary. Last leisure trip was one to three months ago. This destination has some appeal, while other served destinations are also acceptable. Skipping this trip and retaining the ticket money is a credible alternative.
